sentences.text: The applicant has filed this first application u/S 439, Cr.P.C. for grant of bail.

The applicant has been arrested on 02.11.2022 by Police Station Indargarh District Datia (M.P.) in connection with crime No. 254/2022 registered for the offence punishable under Sections 376-D,
323, 506, 34 of IPC.

In brief prosecution case is that on 03.08.2022 prosecutrix a married lady lodged an FIR against present applicant accused and three other co-accused persons alleging that more than two months back present applicant accused telephoned the prosecutrix and called her at Indargarh (Bharoli Gate).
Prosecutrix reached there.
Thereafter, present applicant accused along with co- accused Posham met her and prosecutrix sat between them on their motorcycle.
They took her in secret place when she objected co-accused threatened her with dire consequences.

sentences.text: Present applicant and Posham did rape with her inside the room and other co-accused persons guarding them from outside.
Prosecutrix requested to leaver her, but they didn't.
After sometime, on request of prosecutrix, they left her at the same place from where they took her.
On her complaint crime No. 254/2022 registered for the offence punishable under Sections 376-D, 323, 506, 34 of IPC. was registered at Police Station Indargarh District Datia (M.P.).
After investigation charge-sheet has been filed.
Learned counsel for the applicant argued that applicant is an innocent person and has been falsely implicated.
There is no positive evidence came during medical examination.
It is further submitted that a false FIR has been lodged, if for the sake of argument that can be relied upon, prosecutrix is a married lady aged about 32 years.
Her conduct shows that she is a consenting party.
Beside this, FIR is highly belated more than two months.
The applicant is permanent resident of District Datia (M.P.).
Conclusion of trial is likely to take time and there is no likelihood of his absconsion, if released on bail.
On these grounds, he prays for grant of bail to the applicant.
Learned counsel for the State vehemently opposed the application that he is having criminal history of four cases and co-accused persons are still absconding and prayed for its rejection.

Looking to the aforesaid facts and circumstances of the case, without commenting upon merits of the case, this Court is of the opinion that the application should be allowed and by allowing the application it is ordered that if the applicant furnishes a cash security of Rs.25,000/- along with a personal bail bond of Rs.25,000/- (Rupees Twenty Five Thousand Only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court, he should be released on bail.
He will present during trial before the trial Court on each and every date.
In case of any default, cash security of Rs.25,000/- shall be forfeited without giving any notice.
Application stands allowed and disposed of.
Certified copy as per rules.
